# Notes

https://www.r-bloggers.com/2025/03/the-ellmer-package-for-using-llms-with-r-is-a-game-changer-for-scientists/

Tool use means the LLM can run commands on your computer to retrieve information. You know how LLMs can be bad at simple math like 2+2 or today’s date? Well, with a tool, the LLM would know to use R to calculate this to return the correct answer. Tools can also connect to web APIs, means they can also be used to retrieve information or databases from the web.

You send your question to the LLM as an HTTP request, and it sends back its reply as an HTTP response. In other words, a conversation consists of a sequence of a paired turns: a sent prompt and a returned response.

The `chat()` method does not return any results until the entire response is received. (It can print the streaming results to the console but it returns the result only when the response is complete.)



# Vocabulary

```{r}
"value" = chat_perform_value(provider, req)
"stream" = chat_perform_stream(provider, req)
"async-value" = chat_perform_async_value(provider, req)
"async-stream" = chat_perform_async_stream(provider, req)
```

`value`: 

`stream`: If you want to process the response as it arrives, you can use the `stream()` method. 

`async`: ellmer also supports async usage. This is useful when you want to run multiple, concurrent chat sessions.

The `_async` variants take the same arguments for construction but return a promise instead of the actual response.




# FYI

`Google/Vertex`: Designed for developers / data scientists
`Google/Gemini`: Designed for end-users (general public)

`params()` found in params.R



# Setup for `chat_google_gemini()`
(Found in provider-gemini.R)
```{r}
library(ellmer)
library(httr2)

system_prompt = NULL
base_url = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/"
api_key = NULL
model = NULL
params = NULL
api_args = list()
echo = NULL
```

`system_prompt`: A system prompt to set the behavior of the assistant.
`base_url`: The base URL to the endpoint
`api_key`: API key
`model`: LLM model
`params` : Common model parameters, usually created by `params()`.
`api_args`: Named list of arbitrary extra arguments appended to the body
of every chat API call. 

`echo`: 
* `none`: don't emit any output (default when running in a function).
* `output`: echo text and tool-calling output as it streams in (default     when running at the console).
* `all`: echo all input and output.
------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Utility functions 
(Found in utils.R):

1. `set_default()`
2. `check_echo()`

## Model
```{r}
model <- set_default(model, "gemini-2.0-flash")
```

If `model` argument is not provided (NULL), set model to the `default`, which in our case is `gemini-2.0-flash`. If `model` argument is provided, set to provided value.

Also, `set_default()` will display an informative message: `Using model = "gemini-2.0-flash".` 

* Will use `rlang::caller_arg()` to capture the name of a function argument (model) as a string. `rlang::caller_arg()` is designed for better error reporting. 


## Echo
```{r}
echo <- check_echo(echo)
```

If echo is not provided (`NULL`), code currently executing in a user-facing environment, and is not inside a test, `check_echo()` sets echo to "output". Incidentally, if `echo` argument is set to TRUE, then echo is set to "output". If `echo` argument is FALSE, then "none".

* `env_is_user_facing(parent.frame(2))` is an expression from the `{rlang}` package that checks whether the code is currently executing in a user-facing environment.
* `is_testing()` checks whether code is inside a test.


# Google Credentials 
Found in `provider-gemini.R`
```{r}
credentials <- default_google_credentials(api_key, gemini = TRUE)
```

Grabs `api_key` from Renviron file. Then, sets `credentials` object to a function: `function() {list("x-goog-api-key" = api_key)}`.


# ProviderGoogleGemini (S7 class)
Found in `provider-gemini.R`
```{r}
provider <- ProviderGoogleGemini(
  name = "Google/Gemini",
  base_url = base_url,
  model = model,
  params = params %||% params(),
  extra_args = api_args,
  api_key = api_key,
  credentials = credentials
)
```

`ProviderGoogleGemini` is an S7 class whose parent class is `Provider`, and whose properties are

From `Provider` S7 class:
- `name`: Name of the provider.
- `model`: Name of the model.
- `base_url`: The base URL for the API.
- `params`: A list of standard parameters created by [params()].
- `extra_args`: Arbitrary extra arguments to be included in the request body.

From `ProviderGoogleGemini` S7 class:
- `api_key`: API key for Google Gemini
- `credentials`: `class_function | NULL`, meaning either a function or NULL.
- `model`: Name of model


# Chat (R6 class)
Found in chat.R
```{r}
Chat$new(provider = provider, system_prompt = system_prompt, echo = echo)
```

R6 class initialized with private members:

```{r}
private$provider <- provider
private$echo <- echo
private$callback_on_tool_request <- CallbackManager$new(args = "request")
private$callback_on_tool_result <- CallbackManager$new(args = "result")
self$set_system_prompt(system_prompt)
```

## chat method (from Chat R6 class)
```{r}
chat = function(..., echo = NULL) {
  turn <- user_turn(...)
  echo <- check_echo(echo %||% private$echo)
  
  # Returns a single turn (the final response from the assistant), even if
  # multiple rounds of back and forth happened.
  coro::collect(private$chat_impl(
    turn,
    stream = echo != "none",
    echo = echo
  ))
  
  text <- self$last_turn()@text
  if (echo == "none") text else invisible(text)
}
```

Lets break down this important method line by line (turns.R):
```{r}
turn <- user_turn(...)

# Definition of user_turn()
# Found in turns.R
user_turn <- function(..., .call = caller_env()) {
  as_user_turn(list2(...), call = .call, arg = "...")
}

# Definition of as_user_turn()
as_user_turn <- function(contents, call = caller_env(), arg = "...") {
  if (length(contents) == 0) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg {arg}} must contain at least one input.", call = call)
  }
  if (is_named(contents)) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg {arg}} must be unnamed.", call = call)
  }
  if (S7_inherits(contents, Content)) {
    return(Turn("user", list(contents)))
  }
  
  contents <- lapply(contents, as_content, error_call = call, error_arg = arg)
  Turn("user", contents)
}
```

`as_user_turn()`
- Check whether length of `contents` is 0. If so, signal an error
- Check whether `contents` is named (whether contents has a names attribute). If so, signal an error.
- Apply `as_content()` over a list, `contents`.
- Creates a Turn S7 object. 


`as_content()` (from content.R)
```{r}
as_content <- function(x, error_call = caller_env(), error_arg = "...") {
  if (is.null(x)) {
    list()
  } else if (is_prompt(x)) {
    if (length(x) == 1) {
      ContentText(x[[1]])
    } else {
      cli::cli_abort(
        "{.arg {error_arg}} can only accept a single prompt.",
        call = error_call
      )
    }
  } else if (is.character(x)) {
    ContentText(paste0(x, collapse = "\n\n"))
  } else if (S7_inherits(x, Content)) {
    x
  } else {
    stop_input_type(
      x,
      what = "made up strings or <content> objects",
      arg = error_arg,
      error_call = error_call
    )
  }
}
```

- If `x` is not provided (NULL), return an empty list. 
- If `x` inherits from `ellmer_prompt` class, create a `ContentText` object.
- If `x` is a character, create a `ContentText` object.
- If `x` inherits from Content S7 class, return `x`

Creates a new S7 `ContentText` object, with `text` as its only property.


Echo
```{r}
echo <- check_echo(echo %||% private$echo)
```
If `echo` is not provided (`NULL`), sets echo to "output". 

* `rlang::%||%` is the null-default operator. It returns the left-hand side if it’s not NULL, otherwise it returns the right-hand side.


```{r}
chat_impl = generator_method 
# leads to 
private$submit_turns() # generator method
# leads to
chat_perform()
# leads to
chat_request() # generic
# leads to
req <- base_request(provider) # generic

# Can't use chat_path() because it varies based on stream
req <- req_url_path_append(req, "models")
if (stream) {
  # https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#method:-models.streamgeneratecontent
  req <- req_url_path_append(
    req,
    paste0(provider@model, ":", "streamGenerateContent")
  )
  req <- req_url_query(req, alt = "sse")
} else {
  # https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#method:-models.generatecontent
  req <- req_url_path_append(
    req,
    paste0(provider@model, ":", "generateContent")
  )
}

body <- chat_body(
  provider = provider,
  stream = stream,
  turns = turns,
  tools = tools,
  type = type
)
body <- modify_list(body, provider@extra_args)

req <- req_body_json(req, body)
req
```

`chat_impl` is the 'chat implementation' function that does the heavy lifting behind the user-facing `chat()` method. It is a "generator method".

`submit_turns` is a "generator method" that contains `chat_perform()`, which leads to `chat_request()`

`req <- base_request(provider)` for `provider = ProviderGoogleGemini`
```{r}
method(base_request, ProviderGoogleGemini) <- function(provider) {
  req <- request(provider@base_url) # Create a new HTTP request with provider's base url
  req <- ellmer_req_credentials(req, provider@credentials) # Add headers with credentials (with req_headers())
  req <- req_retry(req, max_tries = 2) # Cap the maximum number of attempts (max_tries) to 2
  req <- ellmer_req_timeout(req, stream) # Set curl option of HTTP timeout to 
  req <- ellmer_req_user_agent(req) # Set user-agent for request
  req <- req_error(req, body = function(resp) {
    json <- resp_body_json(resp, check_type = FALSE) # Extract body from response
    json$error$message
  }) # Control handling of HTTP errors
  req
}
```


```{r}
req <- req_url_path_append(req, "models")
```

Adds `/models` to URL path

```{r}
req <- req_url_path_append(
  req,
  paste0(provider@model, ":", "generateContent")
)
```

Adds `paste0(provider@model, ":", "generateContent")` to path.

```{r}
body <- chat_body(
  provider = provider,
  stream = stream,
  turns = turns,
  tools = tools,
  type = type
)
# leads to
method(chat_body, ProviderGoogleGemini) <- function(
    provider,
    stream = TRUE,
    turns = list(),
    tools = list(),
    type = NULL
) {
  if (length(turns) >= 1 && is_system_prompt(turns[[1]])) {
    system <- list(parts = list(text = turns[[1]]@text))
  } else {
    system <- list(parts = list(text = ""))
  }
  
  generation_config <- chat_params(provider, provider@params)
  if (!is.null(type)) {
    generation_config$response_mime_type <- "application/json"
    generation_config$response_schema <- as_json(provider, type)
  }
  
  contents <- as_json(provider, turns)
  
  # https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#Tool
  if (length(tools) > 0) {
    funs <- as_json(provider, unname(tools))
    tools <- list(functionDeclarations = funs)
  } else {
    tools <- NULL
  }
  
  compact(list(
    contents = contents,
    tools = tools,
    systemInstruction = system,
    generationConfig = generation_config
  ))
}

```
